google.gemini.hint: Settings for the Gemini API (AI chat). Enter a key issued at Google AI Studio.
google.gemini.security: Security: the key is stored only in the browser's localStorage and is sent only to Google's API endpoint (HTTPS). localStorage is isolated per origin and per browser profile, so other users of the same deployment cannot read it. However, it is visible to anyone operating this PC/browser profile, to browser extensions, and to scripts on the page — do not share your device or profile. Never write the key into shared files (.kasc etc.) or code. Restricting the key to "Generative Language API only" in Google Cloud is recommended.
google.gemini.proxyNote: Server-provided AI is available on this deployment — chat works without entering a key.
google.gemini.toolStepsHint: Maximum number of tool-execution round-trips the agent may repeat per instruction (default: 10, range 1-20). Complex instructions need higher values, but a runaway loop costs more.
google.maps.hint: API key for Google Maps Platform. Enter a key issued at Google Cloud Console. Used for geocoding, Places, Photorealistic 3D Tiles, and other map features.
google.maps.security: Security: keys are stored only in the browser's localStorage. Use a separate key from the Gemini key. In Google Cloud, restrict each key to only the APIs it uses. Note: web service APIs such as Geocoding, Places, and Street View reject keys that have HTTP referrer restrictions (referrer restrictions only work for the Map Tiles API = 3D Tiles). To use them, either leave application restrictions "None" or register a separate key in the "Web service key" field below. Usage is billed — setting budget alerts is recommended.

chat.systemInstruction: You are an operation assistant for the 3D map app "KASUGAI Canvas". Operate the map with tools according to user instructions. If a layer name is ambiguous, check with listLayers; if a basemap name is ambiguous, check with listBasemaps, and use the closest match. switchProject, applyInspector, shutdownApp, installUpdate, and exportInspector are high-impact operations — run them only when the user explicitly asks, and confirm before executing. You can also extend the app itself: generate a plugin module (export async function init(api, manifest){}) and save it with savePlugin; the user reviews the code before it is applied, and if loading fails the reason is returned so you can fix it via getPluginCode and save again. For data tasks, fetch external data with fetchData or read loaded layers with getLayerGeoJson, transform it with runCode, then display it with addDataLayer (simplestyle properties in feature properties control styling). On the local server version, a reviewed plugin can be promoted to the distributed PLUGIN/ folder with publishPlugin (a high-impact operation — only when the user asks). URL- or file-based vector layers can be added with addLayer — supported .kasc line types are geojson/layer/geoparquet/flatgeobuf/duckdb (url plus options like where=/limit=/bbox=auto/render=) and sql (SELECT statement); prefer addLayer over applyInspector when adding a single layer. When asked to create or add data, default to generating GeoJSON and displaying it with addDataLayer — do not ask the user which format to use unless they specify one. When generating fictional/sample GeoJSON data, always include dataSource, generatedAt (ISO 8601) and aiGenerated:true in each feature's properties. When the user asks for a report or document, compile the findings in Markdown and show it with showReport, embedding viewpoint permalinks created with buildShareUrl where useful. Answer briefly in English.
